title: Two of M6's three gates on the write-class last-access set are branches no test reaches.
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: Assert.True() Failure at LastAccessGatesAssertionsTests.cs:line 107: "M6's gates on the write-class last-access set are branches no test reaches (2 of 2 unasserted, 342 test units in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests read)", followed by both lines (a) attribute gate and (b) remote gate.
(a) A LastAccessTests Fact sets FileAttributes.Offline on a temp subfolder via TempTree.AddAttributes and asserts LastAccessAsked leaves that folder out while its children are still counted: missing
(a') Deleting `|| (attributes & CloudFolderAttributes) != 0` from Scanner.KeepsLastAccess turns the default suite red: missing
(b) A LastAccessAsked == 0 assertion on a scan of the opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK share: missing
(b') Hard-wiring remote = false in Scanner.DecideLastAccess turns a test red: missing

The slice text asks for 'a LastAccessTests Fact' with Offline. The design ships a three-row Theory whose Offline row is that Fact. A reviewer may prefer the literal single Fact. The spike's per-bit kills are the argument for the Theory.

The remote-gate default-suite assertion lives in ContainerLayerStoreTests' admin-share Fact, which is about the layer store, rather than in a dedicated LastAccessTests share Fact. Reuse was the measured route. A dedicated Fact would be clearer about its subject, but it is unspiked and adds a second admin-share scan.
Whether the admin-share Fact should fail rather than `continue` when no host answers, to make a vacuous mutant-B kill visible. That is left as SL-095's existing semantics and filed.
The SMB-LOOPBACK run and a proof that its new assert bites. It changes machine SMB state and is filed as the person's check; only the spike's sandbox measurement exists.

Rows for RECALL_ON_OPEN and RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS. NTFS drops both bits from user-mode SetFileAttributes, so only the CF-SYNC-ROOT rig could set them. Mutant A is already killed by the three settable bits.
A case for a scan root that itself carries a cloud attribute (the ListRoot caller). It was not named by O-029 and not spiked; filed.
Making the admin-share Facts fail rather than skip when no admin share answers. That changes SL-095's semantics and is filed.
The shifted-gate shape of m5 (two plain subfolders), waived to SC-298.
Any architecture-record edit. This slice makes no sentence of any block untrue.
SC-298: give `off` two plain subfolders (correct count 4, a gate shifted one level reads 3, mutant A reads 5) so a shifted gate is caught.

A person runs the SMB-LOOPBACK filter once under a real user logon (`eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "Network=SMB-LOOPBACK&FullyQualifiedName~StalledShareTests"`) to confirm the new asserts pass unmutated, then checks no \\127.0.0.1\fsa<8hex> mapping remains.
Run the two admin-share Facts, and the mutant B kill, on Windows 10 and on a PC or account where \\localhost\C$ does not answer. There the Facts skip silently and mutant B survives the default suite.
Make the skipped-host branch visible, for example by counting the hosts reached, in the admin-share Facts.
Pin the scan-root caller of the attribute gate (ListRoot, Scanner.cs:241): a scan whose root itself carries OFFLINE, PINNED or UNPINNED.
Assert the RECALL_ON_OPEN and RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS bits through the opt-in CF-SYNC-ROOT rig.
Validate should run Mutants.ps1 once (about 10 minutes for all mutants and both TEMPs, or `-Mutant B -Temp Ordinary` for about 2 minutes) as the check for the mutant cases.

deviation: Mutants.ps1 copies the tree with `git ls-files` (tracked, including uncommitted edits, plus untracked outside .taad and .taad-scratch) instead of the design's `git archive HEAD`. The new tests are uncommitted while the build runs, so an archive of HEAD would not contain them.
deviation: The share asserts are one tuple assertion, `Assert.Equal((0, 0), (x.LastAccessAsked, x.LastAccessKept))`, not four separate Assert.Equal lines. The repro's regex reader accepts the form.

deviation: Added the dedicated LastAccessTests admin-share Fact (accepted finding m4 / O-019) with the ContainerLayerStoreTests asserts kept. Mutant B therefore has two witnesses, and the driver's expected set names both.

deviation: Accepted finding m5 (two plain subfolders under `off`) is not built. Its obligation O-020 was waived and carried to SC-298, so the Theory keeps the design's measured shape: one `off\inner` subfolder, Bytes 4, Asked 3. A gate shifted one level still reads 3 and is not caught yet.

deviation: The corrections for m1 (SYSTEM wording) and m3 (PINNED rationale) belong to the design record (contract, key decision, outside_claims, prior_art), which is outside this repo and cannot be edited by a build. The correct reasoning is in the StalledShareTests remarks and the Theory's remark; the design text itself still carries the old wording.
deviation: Design contract names the repro as `...Tests.csproj`; that file exists and is the one used. The survey's `SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions.csproj` does not exist.

drift: Mutants.ps1 differs from the design's mutant contract in three ways the build did not declare. None of them lets a mutant pass falsely. - It runs `test tests\FsAnalyser.Core.Tests\FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --no-build` after one `build FsAnalyser.slnx --no-incremental` per mutant, not `test FsAnalyser.slnx` per TEMP. That is equivalent today, because Core.Tests is the only test project in the slnx. - The design said a failure outside the expected set is re-run under both TEMPs before anyone calls it a regression. The driver does not re-run; it reports FAIL and lists what went red. A flake such as SynchronousIoCancelTests (lesson #127) therefore makes the driver exit 1, and a person must re-run it.

drift: StalledShareTests puts the new assert at :114, after AssertChildrenAreContiguous as the design placed it. The design's reason, 'so a failure in an existing assertion is still reported first', does not fully hold: the existing `guard.ClosesHandedOff` assertion now comes after it.

drift: Not a departure. The SMB-LOOPBACK assert (StalledShareTests.cs:114) has still never run in this tree. Only the spike's Sandbox measurement (asked 0 unmutated, 3 under B) exists, and it stays the person's check filed by the design.

drift: Nothing new departed in this lens. The round-one drift notes stand. Mutants.ps1 tests the csproj with --no-build after one slnx build per mutant, does not re-run a failure outside the expected set, and StalledShareTests' new assert precedes the existing ClosesHandedOff assertion.

not reached: The SMB-LOOPBACK test on this PC (Windows 11 26200) under the person's own logon. I ran it only in Windows Sandbox 26100.9457 as a local Administrators user via a scheduled task (batch logon). The person's filed check stays: run `eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx --filter "Network=SMB-LOOPBACK&FullyQualifiedName~StalledShareTests"` once; it must pass, and no \\127.0.0.1\fsa<8hex> mapping may remain.
not reached: Windows 10, and any PC or account where \\localhost\C$ does not answer. There both admin-share Facts `continue` silently, and mutant B would survive the default suite (Q-224, case 11).
not reached: Folders with RECALL_ON_OPEN or RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS. User mode cannot set them, and the CF-SYNC-ROOT rig was not run.
not reached: A non-Windows SMB server, such as a NAS running Samba that reports NTFS. Only this PC's own LanmanServer and the SMBLibrary rig were reached.
not reached: That the throughLink assert bites on its own under mutant B. In my runs the Fact stops at the `above` assert first; only the risk spike measured throughLink alone (asked 3).
not reached: The scan-root (ListRoot) case is confirmed only by a scratch probe. No committed test pins it, so a regression there would not turn the suite red (filed by build).

critique missed: Critique M1's fix and the design contract said the mutant driver should `git archive HEAD`. The build adds the new tests uncommitted, so an archive of HEAD cannot contain the tests the mutants must be killed by. The build had to switch to `git ls-files` (tracked plus untracked outside .taad and .taad-scratch). A check would be: 'does the copy method contain the uncommitted files the build is adding?'

critique missed: Critique m4's fix told the builder to add a dedicated Fact scanning `\\{host}\{drive}$\...` without pointing at the private ContainerLayerStoreTests.Loopback helper (:821) that already builds that path. The build wrote a character-for-character copy at LastAccessTests.cs:161. Two default-suite witnesses of mutant B then carry separate copies of one path rule (SC-299). A check would be: 'when a new test builds a path that another test class already builds, name the shared helper'.

critique missed: M1 asked for a scratch-copy driver under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp that takes about 10 minutes. It did not ask what happens when the process is killed before its `finally`. Q-222 (the engine's 120 s case-runner kill), lesson #132 (851 leaked fsa-* dirs) and the 10-minute tool cap were all in the handed context. A killed run leaves about 150 MB under fsa-sl102-mutants-<8hex> and nothing sweeps it (R2-m2, SC-300).

critique missed: M1's driver spec required `git diff --exit-code src` = 0 at the end without asking what happens when src is already dirty at the start. Any later slice that edits Scanner.cs near the gates and re-runs Mutants.ps1 exits 1 with a message that reads as worktree contamination (R2-m3, SC-301). The header comment also wrongly claims dirty-start support.

still unknown: Does the remote-gate witness hold on a PC or account where \\localhost\C$ does not answer (Windows 10, a non-admin account, UAC remote restrictions on loopback)? There both admin-share Facts skip silently and mutant B survives the default suite. Only Mutants.ps1 fails, from an empty red set (Q-224, validate case 11).

still unknown: Does the new StalledShareTests assert (StalledShareTests.cs:114) pass under the person's own logon on the Windows 11 26200 host? Validate ran it only in a 26100.9457 Sandbox as a local user through a scheduled-task batch logon.

still unknown: Does any real folder ever carry RECALL_ON_OPEN or RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS? U-004 found no directory with a RECALL bit in a standalone exe, so the CF-SYNC-ROOT follow-up for those two bits may guard code that never fires on folders.

still unknown: Does a server that reports 'NTFS' but is not Windows, such as a Samba NAS, still make FileRemoteProtocolInfo succeed on the redirector handle? Only this PC's LanmanServer and the SMBLibrary rig were reached.

still unknown: Does the throughLink assert in the admin-share Fact bite on its own under mutant B? In the committed Fact it stops at the `above` assert first; only the risk spike measured throughLink alone (asked 3).

went wrong: Critique ran twice. Pass 1 halted with 6 findings, including a major (M1): the slice's real criteria, (a') and (b') mutant kills, were discharged only by hand edits in an uncommitted scratch copy. The cause was upstream. The repro command was a regex source reader that passes on StalledShareTests alone, so it could not express the criteria, and the design inherited the gap.

went wrong: The survey stage wrote mutant B into the real worktree's Scanner.cs through a relative path in a hand script. It was reverted with `git checkout` and that run's results were discarded. This was the very risk the design later listed as an unproven precondition.

went wrong: The design record carried claims that were wrong or would not compile. It said the engine runs as SYSTEM (only the Sandbox does), that PINNED is missing from Kernel32 (Kernel32.cs:31-32 defines it), and that a dedicated share Fact was 'unspiked' (the investigation probe had measured it). Two Theory lines did not compile (CS0176 and a uint/FileAttributes `&`/`==` precedence error). Build cannot edit the design record, so the old wording is still there.

went wrong: Code review ran twice and found the duplicated admin-share path rule, a kill-leak and a dirty-src false failure in Mutants.ps1. It also found undeclared departures: no rerun of out-of-set failures, per-mutant `build` plus csproj `test --no-build`, and an assert placed before the existing ClosesHandedOff assertion, which breaks the design's stated reason for its position. The three minors were waived to SC-299, SC-300 and SC-301 rather than fixed.

went wrong: The shifted-gate hole (critique m5) was accepted as real but waived to SC-298, so the Theory's Asked == 3 still cannot tell 'off skipped' from 'off\inner skipped'. A green Mutants.ps1 therefore does not prove the gate is per-folder.

went wrong: Part of the build's evidence predates the final shape. The 22/22 filtered run and the 874/874 'as shipped' run were taken before the Theory's tree was trimmed. The final shape is covered only by the driver's baseline, not by those two runs.
went wrong: Validate ran twice only because attempt 1 was turned away by the provider's session limit. That is no quality signal, but a gate stage was lost to infrastructure.

went wrong: Some checks remain unreached. The SMB-LOOPBACK assert on the host's own logon, Windows 10, an admin-share-less PC, the RECALL bits and a committed ListRoot test were all not reached or not built. The default suite protects the remote gate only on a PC whose admin share answers.
